title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 49
paragraphs: The herald, having spoken thus, waited some time; and then, as no one answered him, he departed and went back. On his return he reported to Mardonius what had happened to him. Mardonius, greatly rejoiced and elated by his empty victory, sent the cavalry to attack the Greeks. And when the horsemen rode up to attack, they damaged the whole Greek army by hurling javelins and shooting arrows, being mounted archers and therefore hard to fight against; they also disturbed and choked up the spring Gargaphia, from which the whole Greek army was drawing its water. Now the Lacedaemonians alone were posted near this spring, and it was at some distance from the rest of the Greeks (each being posted where they happened to be), while the Asopos was close at hand; but when they were kept away from the Asopos, they would go back and forth to this spring — for the horsemen and archers prevented them from fetching water from the river.
